primary_task: Implement a feature or bug fix test-first: write a failing test, run it and watch it fail, write minimal code to pass, then run the project's full test suite and report results.

requirements.name: shell
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session; network requests reach only the allow-listed hosts"

requirements.name: project test runner (npm test | pytest | cargo test)
requirements.evidence: run the project's test command (bare `pytest`, `npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task named only one test file
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts ..."

requirements.name: read/write/edit files
requirements.evidence: Write one minimal test showing what should happen. ... Write simplest code to pass the test.
requirements.basis: "write": "create and overwrite files"; "edit": "edit existing files and Jupyter notebooks"

requirements.name: ask_user
requirements.basis: "ask_user": "ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation"

notes: The test runner depends on the repository's language; the document lists pytest, npm test and cargo test as alternatives (one requirement). All are obtainable from open registries (PyPI, npm, apt / GitHub). If a repo's test suite itself needed Docker, a GPU or external credentials, that would be a repo property not stated in the document; under that other reading the verdict could change, but the document does not say so.
